posts.name: 43-world-energy-drinks-heart-reports
posts.caption:
Energy drinks and stimulant supplements show up in 11 times more cardiac arrest reports in a US safety database. That does not mean your risk is 11 times higher ⚡

University of Virginia researchers compared 854 reports on caffeine and stimulant products with 27,491 reports on other foods and supplements (2017 to 2025). Cardiac arrest, heart attack and chest pain came up far more often, and about 45% of the heart reports involved people aged 18 to 34. The reports are voluntary, so nobody knows how many people drank these products with no problem, and the study cannot show cause. For context, the American Heart Association says most adults can generally have up to 400 mg of caffeine a day.

Source: Sai Samayamanthula, study author (University of Virginia School of Medicine), “Energy drinks, stimulant products linked to cardiac arrest, heart attack in young adults”, American Heart Association Scientific Sessions, 2026 (conference abstract, not peer-reviewed yet).
